a.z: 魔術師的戲法天衣無縫。
a.y: The magician's trick was flawless.

a.z: 公司的補償方案合情合理，大家都能接受。
a.y: The company's compensation plan was fair and reasonable, and everyone could accept it.

e: there's more to this than meets the eye
事有蹊蹺.u: 蹊蹺 (qī qiāo) means odd and suspicious; usually leads to an investigation or doubt.

他山之石，可以攻錯.d: Stones from other hills can polish jade: learn from others to improve oneself.
x: 他山之石，可以攻錯，我們不妨研究新加坡的交通管理。

s.d: Teaching and learning go hand in hand.
s.z: 教學相長，教書讓我學到的，和學生學到的一樣多。
s.y: Teaching has taught me as much as it has taught my students. I truly learn from teaching.

s.z: 好的教學和好奇心相輔相成。
s.y: Good teaching and curiosity complement each other.

a.z: 做產品不能閉門造車，要多聽用戶意見。
a.y: You can't build products in isolation; listen to your users.

a.z: 公司墨守成規，難以創新。
a.y: The company sticks to old rules and finds it hard to innovate.

e: take a leaf out of sb's book
use others' successes as a benchmark
他山之石，可以攻錯.u: From the Book of Songs (Xiao Ya, He Ming); also 他山之石，可以攻玉; used to suggest drawing on others' experience.

醍醐灌頂.d: An aha moment; sudden, complete enlightenment.
x: 她的講課令我如醍醐灌頂，終於弄懂了這個理論。

s.z: 一切突然豁然開朗，真是靈光乍現的一刻。
s.y: Everything suddenly became clear. It was a real eureka moment.

s.z: 經歷生死關頭後，他大徹大悟，明白人生真正重要的是什麼。
s.y: After his near-death experience, he was wide awake to what truly mattered in life.

a.z: 這張表格讓我一頭霧水。
a.y: I'm baffled by this form.

a.z: 系統為什麼一直當機，我百思不解。
a.y: I'm flummoxed by why the system keeps crashing.

醍醐灌頂.u: Usually with 如; the listed mind-blowing stresses shock, while the Chinese is about insight.

x: 這場工作坊幫助團隊在規劃上突破盲點。

e: sometimes it takes an outsider to fully appreciate something
s.d: Outsiders see more clearly; help from others.
s.z: 有時旁觀者清，局外人才看得清問題。
s.y: Sometimes it takes an outsider to see the problem clearly.

s.p: tā shān zhī shí, kě yǐ gōng cuò
s.z: 他山之石，可以攻錯，我們不妨研究新加坡的交通管理。
s.y: Studying how Singapore manages traffic gave us a useful benchmark; stones from other hills can polish our own jade.

e: can't see the forest for the trees
be too close to the situation
a.d: Too close to the situation to see it clearly.
a.z: 他太投入了，當局者迷，沒發現問題。
a.y: He is so deep in it that he can't see the forest for the trees.

a.d: Working behind closed doors, ignoring outside input.
a.z: 做產品不能閉門造車，要多聽用戶意見。
a.y: You can't build products in isolation; listen to your users.

e: see what one has been missing
突破盲點.u: 盲點 is a problem one isn't aware of; common in management and learning.

x: 我在心裡暗記了那輛車的車牌。

s.z: 她的建議，我會謹記在心。
s.y: Her advice will be taken to heart.

e: have sth constantly on one's mind
s.d: Always having it on one's mind.
s.z: 即將到來的考試，是她念茲在茲的事。
s.y: The coming exam is something she constantly has on her mind.

e: put sth out of one's mind
a.d: Putting something out of one's mind.
a.z: 他把老師的叮嚀全拋諸腦後。
a.y: He put the teacher's advice completely out of his mind.

a.z: 榮華富貴不過是過眼雲煙。
a.y: Wealth and glory are no more than passing clouds.

e: make a mental note of sth
心裡暗記.u: For noting important information, often quietly so no one knows.

心領神會.d: Getting the message without being told.
x: 我們互看一眼，彼此心領神會。

s.z: 他們之間心照不宣。
s.y: There was a tacit understanding between them.

s.z: 他們多年搭檔，心有靈犀。
s.y: After years as partners, they are on the same wavelength.

a.z: 這張表格讓我一頭霧水。
a.y: I'm baffled by this form.

e: not understand what is going on
a.z: 大家都不明所以，只好等他解釋。
a.y: Everyone was baffled and had to wait for his explanation.

e: get the message without being told
心領神會.u: Also for grasping ideas or moods. 心領了 (a polite refusal: "thank you, but no") is a different expression.

信以為真.d: Taking something at face value; falling for it.
x: 她把那則傳聞信以為真。

s.z: 她對學生深信不疑。
s.y: She has an unshakable faith in her students.

s.z: 他對別人的批評照單全收。
s.y: He accepts all the criticism without pushback.

e: take sth. with a grain of salt
a.z: 他的承諾，我聽了半信半疑。
a.y: I took his promise with a grain of salt.

a.z: 這件案子疑點重重，必須重新調查。
a.y: The case is full of doubts and must be re-investigated.

信以為真.u: Usually about being misled; implies being too trusting.

心有戚戚焉.d: It strikes a chord with me.
x: 聽她說起童年，我心有戚戚焉。

s.d: Feeling someone's pain as one's own.
s.z: 她的故事讓我感同身受，字字都像在說我。
s.y: Her story was so relatable that I felt every word as if it were my own.

s.d: Seeing things from the other person's side.
s.z: 批評她之前，先將心比心。
s.y: Try to put yourself in her shoes before you criticize.

a.z: 事不關己，他選擇袖手旁觀。
a.y: It was none of his business, so he stood by and did nothing.

e: be like a fish out of water
a.z: 在古板的辦公室裡，那位年輕設計師顯得格格不入。
a.y: He felt like a fish out of water among his new colleagues.

心有戚戚焉.u: From Mencius (King Hui of Liang I), King Xuan's response to Mencius; now means "that's exactly how I feel."

x: 他們之間心照不宣。

s.d: Getting the message without being told.
s.z: 我們互看一眼，彼此心領神會。
s.y: We exchanged a look and grasped each other's meaning intuitively.

s.z: 健康的飲食會帶來更健康的生活，這是不言而喻的。
s.y: It is self-evident that a healthy diet leads to a healthier life.

a.z: 兩位領導人開誠布公地談了彼此的分歧。
a.y: The two leaders spoke in full transparency about their differences.

a.z: 她直截了當地說出了自己的想法。
a.y: She said exactly what she thought without beating around the bush.

心照不宣.u: Often implies something that can't be said openly; stresses not saying it more than 心領神會.

x: 她一反常態地遲到了。

s.z: 改編後的劇情面目全非。
s.y: After the adaptation, the plot is unrecognizable.

s.z: 他參加培訓後，判若兩人。
s.y: After the training, he was like a different person.

a.z: 她對朋友始終如一，從不因對方失勢而改變態度。
a.y: She treated her friends the same throughout and never changed when they fell on hard times.

a.z: 課程並非一成不變。
a.y: The curriculum is not set in stone.

一反常態.u: Used as an adverb; implies "not usually like this," often sparking curiosity or concern.

x: 比賽結果令人意料之外。

s.z: 突然的宣布出乎意料，大家都愣住了。
s.y: The sudden announcement took everyone by surprise.

s.z: 疫情的規模令專家始料未及。
s.y: The scale of the epidemic was something experts never anticipated.

a.z: 球隊輸球並不意外，是意料之中。
a.y: The team's loss came as no surprise.

a.z: 不出所料，開學第一天列車又誤點了。
a.y: Predictably, the train was late again on the first day of school.

意料之外.u: Usually a noun phrase: 在意料之外 or 意料之外的結果; plainer and less surprised than 出乎意料.

x: 把責任推給前任經理是意料中事，沒人感到意外。

s.z: 不出所料，開學第一天列車又誤點了。
s.y: Predictably, the train was late again on the first day of school.

s.z: 球隊輸球並不意外，是意料之中。
s.y: The team's loss came as no surprise.

a.z: 突然的宣布出乎意料，大家都愣住了。
a.y: The sudden announcement took everyone by surprise.

a.z: 那支弱隊奪冠，讓我跌破眼鏡。
a.y: I was incredulous when the underdog won the championship.

意料中事.u: Often implies resignation or indifference: "I knew it would happen."

x: 袖口上的污漬，一望便知他剛才在刷油漆。

s.z: 這張圖表一目了然。
s.y: The chart is clear at a glance.

s.z: 他根本沒在聽，這再顯而易見不過了。
s.y: It was beyond obvious that he wasn't listening.

a.d: Bewildering; hard to tell true from false.
a.z: 案情撲朔迷離，警方一時理不出頭緒。
a.y: The case is baffling, and the police cannot yet make sense of it.

a.z: 音調的變化微小到幾乎難以察覺。
a.y: The change in pitch was almost imperceptible.

一望便知.u: Stresses judging at a single glance, more than 一目了然; often with clues.

x: 他想在北極賣冰，真是異想天開。

s.z: 他想坐竹筏橫渡大洋，簡直癡人說夢。
s.y: His plan to cross the ocean on a raft is wildly unrealistic.

s.z: 這個故事荒誕不經，沒人會信。
s.y: The story is absurd, and nobody will believe it.

a.z: 他是個腳踏實地的人，穩穩地持續前進。
a.y: He is a down-to-earth man who stays grounded and keeps pushing ahead.

a.z: 做研究要實事求是，不能先有結論再找證據。
a.y: Research should seek truth from facts, not start from a conclusion and look for evidence.

異想天開.u: Usually mocking; occasionally praises a vivid imagination.

x: 這位小說家彷彿能預見未來，在網路出現前幾十年就描寫了它。

s.z: 她洞燭機先，早在股市崩盤前就看出端倪。
s.y: She could see it coming long before the market crashed.

s.z: 她提早賣出，事後證明很有先見之明。
s.y: Her decision to sell early proved prescient.

a.z: 他是事後諸葛，比賽結束後什麼答案都有。
a.y: He's a Monday morning quarterback who has all the answers after the game.

a.z: 這個決定目光短淺。
a.y: The decision was short-sighted.

預見未來.u: Can mean predicting or prophecy, or simply foresight; often praises long-term vision.

x: 真沒想到，一開門，全班同學捧著蛋糕在等我。

s.z: 突然的宣布出乎意料，大家都愣住了。
s.y: The sudden announcement took everyone by surprise.

s.z: 疫情的規模令專家始料未及。
s.y: The scale of the epidemic was something experts never anticipated.

a.z: 球隊輸球並不意外，是意料之中。
a.y: The team's loss came as no surprise.

a.z: 不出所料，開學第一天列車又誤點了。
a.y: Predictably, the train was late again on the first day of school.

真沒想到.u: Colloquial, often at the start of a sentence, for pleasant or unpleasant surprises.

x: 他的真知灼見，幫團隊看清了真正的問題。

e: hit the nail on the head
s.d: Hitting the nail on the head.
s.z: 你這句話一針見血，點出了問題所在。
s.y: You hit the nail on the head with that comment.

s.z: 一位好的領導者必須高瞻遠矚。
s.y: A good leader must take the long view.

e: have only a smattering of knowledge
a.z: 他對這個主題一知半解。
a.y: He has only a smattering of knowledge about the issue, yet loves to give his opinion.

a.d: Trotting out the same old tune.
a.z: 這場演說只是老調重彈。
a.y: The speech just rehashed old arguments.

真知灼見.u: Praise for someone's views; common in reviews and speeches.

x: 比賽輸了之後，教練做了深刻的自我反省。

s.d: Regretting what one did; about regret.
s.z: 他悔不當初，後悔簽了那份合約。
s.y: He rues the day he signed that contract.

s.z: 他出獄後洗心革面，重新做人。
s.y: After his release he turned over a new leaf and started afresh.

a.z: 他自以為是，認為自己比誰都懂。
a.y: He thinks he knows best and never listens to anyone.

e: bury one's head in the sand
a.z: 假裝什麼事都沒有，只是自欺欺人。
a.y: Pretending nothing is wrong is just burying your head in the sand.

自我反省.u: Often 深刻的自我反省 (deep self-reflection); positive, implying growth.

x: 他靠自主學習，自己學會了寫程式。

s.z: 他無師自通，自己學會了寫程式。
s.y: He is self-taught and learned to code on his own.

s.z: 她求知若渴，整夜都在閱讀。
s.y: She has a thirst for knowledge and reads every day.

a.z: 公司墨守成規，難以創新。
a.y: The company sticks to old rules and finds it hard to innovate.

a.z: 別囫圇吞棗，要質疑你讀到的東西。
a.y: Don't swallow information whole; question what you read.

自主學習.u: An education term; stresses taking the initiative and planning one's own learning. The listed autodidactic is rare; self-directed is the usual term.
